title: Directions (Q1–3): Read the passage and answer the questions
passage:
Ocean currents are driven by two broad mechanisms. Wind-driven currents occupy the upper few hundred metres and are organised into large gyres by the Coriolis effect and the shape of the ocean basins.

Thermohaline circulation, in contrast, is driven by differences in water density, which depends on temperature and salinity. Cold, salty water at high latitudes sinks and spreads slowly along the ocean floor. Together, the two systems carry heat from the tropics towards the poles and influence regional climate.

questions.question: According to the passage, what mainly drives the thermohaline circulation?
Which kind of current is organised into large gyres?
What is the combined effect of the two systems, as stated in the passage?

options.B: They carry heat from the tropics towards the poles
